title: Personal Tech Support 24/7 | HP SmartFriend | HP
description: Get personalized support at any time, for any brand of PC or tablet, with HP SmartFriend. asr.full_text: Music I'm John at HPSmart Friends Service's Call Center. Think of me and my fellow HPSmart friends as your personal help desk, your tech gurus. How can I help you today? I've been working on my family tree, and I thought I saved it, but it just disappeared! What do I do? Losing anything of personal value can be frustrating. The good news is that it can be recovered, and sometimes it takes some serious digging, but we get it done. Yeah, hi, I just got one of those virus alerts. It says click here. Should I click it? The first rule I always tell people is never click on anything if you are unsure. Pick up the phone, call us, and we'll determine the next steps. Now they're asking me for my passwords, and I'm just not sure about this. Would you mind if I connect to your computer remotely so I can see what's going on? You can do that? What do I do? Just sit back and relax. If a virus is present, we'll work to clean that up first, and then help protect you against identity theft. It's not all of Fire Drills. We help people get the most out of their technology. And teach them how to sync all of their different devices. This is John at HP Smart Friends Services. How can I help you today? I go to All My Suns games and I take a million videos. The problem is the videos are stuck in my phone, but I want to transfer them to my tablet. I can help with that. Customers with monthly subscriptions to HP Smart Friend services can call as often as they want. I heard that you can print photos directly from your phone. How do I do that? Some people call a lot. A lot a lot. We give them confidence and peace of mind. That was easy. Thank you. You did it. Thanks. Thank you so much. Transcription by ESO. Translation by —

textual.observation: A user describes a virus alert that requests a click and then asks for passwords; the representative advises against clicking when unsure and offers to determine next steps.

evidence.quote: It says click here. Should I click it?
Now they're asking me for my passwords, and I'm just not sure about this.
The first rule I always tell people is never click on anything if you are unsure.

textual.context: The mechanism is presented in a scripted support-warning dialogue. The representative explicitly discourages clicking; the source does not establish whether the alert or password request was genuine.
textual.potential_relevance: A suspicious alert links a requested click and password submission to a stated virus scenario, creating a concrete mechanism for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not identify the alert's sender or destination, establish whether any password was submitted, or show an actual outcome. No visual evidence is supplied.

textual_context_notes.observation: The representative warns the audience not to click when uncertain and recommends calling support to determine next steps.

evidence.quote: Pick up the phone, call us, and we'll determine the next steps.
The first rule I always tell people is never click on anything if you are unsure.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents HP SmartFriend as a paid technical-support service offering help with computer problems and device synchronization. The password request and virus alert are presented as a customer's reported situation, while the representative advises against clicking uncertain content and recommends contacting support. The suspicious mechanism is therefore used in a support-warning dialogue rather than as an instruction to click, submit a password, or transfer money.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The main content promotes an ordinary technical-support service, including support for PCs and tablets and a sign-up prompt. The transcript also describes monthly subscriptions to the support service; this does not establish a paid earning-guidance offer.
